PC1_FULL_DOM_DISCRIMINATION.description: Full DOM chi-squared test across page types

NC1_SAMPLE_INVARIANCE.description: Locatable_sample tag composition identical within each page type
NC1_SAMPLE_INVARIANCE.observed: Within-type std = 0.0 for all metrics (PASS for within-type invariance). Between-type eta2 = 1.0 (FAIL for zero eta2).
NC1_SAMPLE_INVARIANCE.note: Null control passes: within-type variance IS zero. But between-type variance is perfect (eta2=1.0), which means the sample DOES have task-type structure.

observations: OBS-1: The locatable_sample is NOT a fixed template across ALL tasks. Y-coordinates of elements 12-19 differ within each page type (8 differences per multi-task type). However, tags, roles, inForm flags, x-coordinates, widths, and heights are 100% identical within each page type.

OBS-2: Structural template identity (without y): listing tasks share identical structural composition (7 tags, 85% inForm, total area 341795). Detail tasks share identical composition (7 tags, 95% inForm, total area 589190). Cart has unique composition (7 tags, 95% inForm, total area 428790).

OBS-3: The sample DOES have task-type discrimination: eta-squared = 1.0 for tag entropy, form fraction, total area, and mean bbox area. This means 100% of variance in these metrics is between-page-type, not within. The sample is NOT informationally zero.

OBS-4: Within-type standard deviation is 0.0 for all sample metrics within each page type. All listing tasks produce identical metrics; all detail tasks produce identical metrics. This confirms the sample is a fixed template WITHIN each page type.

OBS-5: Full DOM tag counts differ dramatically across page types: listing has 501 div/1204 a/1492 span; detail has 322 div/985 a/1053 span; cart has 43 div/320 a/319 span. Chi-squared p = 6.14e-53 confirms significant differences.

OBS-6: Mutual information I(tag_composition; page_type) = 1.449 bits for BOTH locatable_sample and full DOM. The sample carries the same task-type information as the full DOM for the 7-task/3-type dataset.
OBS-7: checkout_1 tasks (2 entries) have error 'Page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED' and are excluded from analysis. cart_1 appears twice (duplicate entry); deduplicated to single task.
validity_notes: VN-1: Small sample: 7 tasks (3 listing, 3 detail, 1 cart), 1 Magento site, 3 definitions. No checkout data available. Cross-site generalization not tested.
VN-2: checkout_1 excluded due to connection refused error. Cart has only 1 task, so within-type template identity cannot be tested for cart.

VN-3: The parent's FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING was based on hierarchy-weighted density eta2=0.0. This experiment shows the sample HAS task-type structure (eta2=1.0 on basic metrics), so the parent's zero eta2 was specific to the density metric, not a property of the sample.

VN-4: Mutual information is identical for sample and full DOM (1.449 bits) because with 3 page types, the maximum MI is log2(3)=1.585 bits, and the discrete feature representation captures most of it.

VN-5: The y-coordinate differences in elements 12-19 reflect different page content lengths (listing pages have varying numbers of products, pushing footer elements to different vertical positions). These are positional, not structural differences.
unresolved: U-1: The template explanation for zero density eta2 is FALSIFIED. The parent's density failure is NOT due to sample template invariance. Why did the hierarchy-weighted density produce eta2=0.0 if the sample has clear task-type structure? The specific density formula may map different sample compositions to the same density value.

U-2: Could a different density metric (not hierarchy-weighted) capture the task-type structure present in the sample? The sample has eta2=1.0 on entropy/form_frac/total_area, suggesting density metrics based on these features would work.
U-3: The 31x canonical/weighted material gap (EXP-INTEL-35264637598) remains valid. The question is whether a density metric can be designed to exploit the task-type structure in the sample.
U-4: Cross-site generalization of sample template identity is untested. Different Magento sites may have different sample compositions.
